utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Ekkehard Withopf, and the case manager, Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. And for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Madam Judge. Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. President. Representing General Hadzihasanovic is Mr. Alexis Demirdjian and myself, Stephane Bourgon. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura for today, Mr. Rodney Dixon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber bids good morning to all those present, Mr. Withopf, Mr. Mundis, the three attorneys for the accused, the accused, as well as the registrar, who we see has come back - with pleasure we welcome him - as well as the usher of this courtroom and all the staff in the courtroom, the court reporter, the interpreters, and the assistant, without of course forgetting the security officers. We need today to continue with the examination-in-chief of the witness. But before bringing the witness in, I want to make it quite clear to avoid any confusion that we addressed yesterday the question of documents which will be examined at a hearing specially devoted to documents. That hearing, in the opinion of the Chamber, should not take longer than one week, which means that it should take place over five days on the outside. Perhaps less, but not beyond one week. And that is why I told Mr. Withopf yesterday that one should plan that week either one week prior to General Reinhardt's testimony or a week after his testimony so that there should be no confusion regarding the scheduling of these hearings. So on the outside five days, as a minimum three or four days. That will obviously depend on the positions of both parties. In order to ensure the smooth conduct of the proceedings, it was already indicated yesterday but I wish to remind you all of it, that the Prosecutor will produce their document explaining the document with arguments of the relevance of that document for the Prosecution and in relation to the pre-trial brief requesting the admission of that document by the Prosecution. After that, which will probably take a few minutes only, after that submission, the Defence will make their observations, which of course also have to be concise, for it will not be possible to have -- to spend hours over a single document. Therefore, you must concentrate yourself on the objections you have and present them in roughly the same amount of time as the Prosecution takes, if there are objections. Of course, you will have time to familiarise yourself with those documents and to finalise your position. We will do this for the documents that may cause problems, and we will deal with them document by document. That is why we have suggested that categories of documents be formed by the 19th of April according to the criteria that I referred to. The Chamber just wished to add these few words to the ruling made yesterday. Mr. Usher, will you bring the witness in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you hearing the translation well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please take a seat.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall give the floor to Mr. Withopf, who is going to continue with his questions for you as part of his examination-in-chief, which he started yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Withopf: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, whilst you've been in Zenica in 1993 and in 1994, did you get to know who the commander or the commanders of the ABiH 3rd Corps have been?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During my time, it was first of all General Hadzihasanovic, followed by General Alagic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the point in time as to when General Hadzihasanovic was followed by General Alagic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was sometime in November. I think it was mid-November that he handed over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, did you get a chance to get to know General Hadzihasanovic yourself?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We had quite a number of meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did this meeting take place on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on a regular basis from the point of view of a set time or a set day. It was more as required, when there was something that I needed to raise or General Hadzihasanovic needed to raise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did these meetings take place?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were his headquarters located at the time?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were located in Zenica, not very far from where we were based.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, did you get to know about General Hadzihasanovic's previous military career prior to having joined the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he had served in the JNA, the Yugoslav National Army, but I was not aware of the details of exactly where he had served or what he had done in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on what you got to know, Sir Martin, and based on what you have seen and heard, and based on your knowledge having served as an officer in the British Army for 37 years, what do you think about the professionalism of Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: He always gave the impression to me of being a thoroughly professional soldier, and my understanding was he was absolutely clear and straight in his dealings with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in power?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was clear he had authority in 3 Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in command and in control over his units subordinated to 3 Corps?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, yes. Perhaps I should add in parentheses here that I had always had a slightly uneasy feeling that both the HVO, the Croat army, and the ABiH, because they were so young and so new - they'd only been running for about a year - I had doubts about some of the lower-level commanders and quality of the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whenever you had the chance to talk to Hadzihasanovic - and I understand such meetings took place repeatedly - did you get the impression that Hadzihasanovic was informed what was going on in the field?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, he always gave me the impression of being very well aware of what was going on throughout his whole area of command. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please give us an example or examples.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot -- it's difficult to give specific examples, but whenever I asked questions, I would get what I believed to be straight answers. And, for example, although I was not deliberately checking up on what he said, if I went to the headquarters of General Alagic, who was then commanding the operational zone based in Travnik, I would hear similar stories which tied in with what General Hadzihasanovic had told me, which was I believed corroboration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, did you get to know at the time who Hadzihasanovic's deputy was?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a man called Dzemal Merdan, who I believe had been formerly a naval officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A naval officer within the JNA?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of your meetings and discussions with Hadzihasanovic, was the issue of the military discipline discussed?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it came up specifically at a meeting when we had Ambassador De Baans, who was the Belgian head of the mission at that time, and we were discussing amongst other things discipline. And I think as Ambassador De Baans asked General Hadzihasanovic whether he was satisfied with the discipline in his corps, in his forces, and the reply was yes, he was; but then he said, "Is any commander fully satisfied with the discipline of his forces?" And he made the comment, was the commander of the British Battalion satisfied with the discipline throughout his full battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who at the time was the commander of the BritBat battalion?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Lieutenant Colonel Alastair Duncan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, I am now going to show you a document. It is an ECMM report of 3 November 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: For the information of the Trial Chamber and Defence, this document has been marked for identification as P181 by a decision of the Trial Chamber of 2nd of April. It's a document which is not contested by Defence, obviously. Unfortunately, Sanction is not working today for technical reasons. We, however, have the respective numbers of photocopies available in both English and B/C/S. The French translation will follow at a later point, once it is available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, if you could please have a look at the document and first, please, identify who is the originator of this document.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I clearly wrote this report myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber, Sir Martin, can you please have a look at the first page and explain the abbreviations at the very top of this page.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The -- right at the very top it is HRC Zenica, which stands for the head of the regional centre Zenica, and that at the time was me. And then it's addressed to HCC Mostar and HCC Travnik, head of the coordinating centre Mostar and head of the coordinating centre Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Sir Martin. Sir Martin, if I may draw your attention, please, to page 8 of this document. And on page 8, to paragraph 9. This is the paragraph which starts with the words "When asked whether he was satisfied with the discipline in 3rd Corps ...."

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this paragraph, Sir Martin, does it reflect the conversation with Hadzihasanovic you were just informing the Trial Chamber about?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution wishes to tender this document into evidence and be given a final Prosecution exhibit number, please. Can the witness please keep this document, since later on I will have additional questions in relation to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. The number was P121 marked for identification, so it should become 181. It's a document recognised and identified by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is a document regarding which we have already commented on. It can be admitted into the file. But we wish to note that documents of this kind, consisting of several pages -- in our opinion we need to judge the probative value of these documents regarding certain paragraphs but not regarding the entire content of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is an uncontested document, so it should be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Continue, Mr. Withopf. Mr. Registrar, will you give us the final number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the English version gets the exhibit number P181, and the B/C/S translation gets the exhibit number P181/BCS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, in the course of meetings and discussions with Hadzihasanovic, was the issue of the Mujahedin ever raised?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I used to raise it regularly when I had meetings with Bosniak leaders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Including General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Including General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you and/or General Hadzihasanovic actually use the word "Mujahedin"?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure I would have done. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the course of such meetings and discussions, what was discussed from your side and/or from Hadzihasanovic's side in respect to the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was always very interested and concerned about the Mujahedin, and so I used to ask what was the situation. It was quite clear that General Hadzihasanovic and his successor did not like the Mujahedin. They used to say that there were a few who were fighting well for the Bosniaks but there were others who, clearly, they would wish to have out of their area. However, the impression always given to me was that they considered that they had them under control, that they were under command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, I'm now going to show you a further document, please. This is the ECMM report of the 29th of October, 1993. The respective numbers of photocopies are available in English, B/C/S, and they are also available in its French translations. Sir Martin, can you please first identify for the benefit of the Trial Chamber who drafted this document.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was clearly sent out by William Stutt, the head of the coordinating centre Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you told us yesterday, Sir Martin - and you informed the Trial Chamber about the way and the manner such documents were put together, and they were discussed prior to being sent out and they were discussed with you, and you gave approval for such documents - do you consider yourself being in a position to comment on the contents of this document?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I could just clarify one point. This was a document sent to my headquarters, and therefore I would not have had any say in this before we received it as a report, because this is a report coming to my headquarters from HCC Travnik, which would then be incorporated or parts of it would be incorporated into the RC Zenica report, which would be sent off to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would just like to learn from my learned friend what is the number of this document on the list of documents, because I have three documents with this date and it doesn't appear to follow the order 1, 2, 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: For the information of the Trial Chamber and my learned friend from the Defence, this has been marked for identification by a decision of the Trial Chamber of 2nd of April with the ID number P178.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, if you could please have a look again at the first page, at the very top. And for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, can you please very briefly explain what the abbreviations do mean.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The HQ Zagreb HUM stands for the headquarters of the ECMM and addressed HUM is -- it would go to the humanitarian cell in the headquarters. CC Mostar was the coordinating centre Mostar. CC Tuzla, the coordinating centre Tuzla. ECLO Kiseljak was the EC liaison officer at Kiseljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Wait. Stop. [Interpretation] We're obliged to stop for about ten minutes because there's a technical problem. So we are going to have a ten-minute break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now resume. Mr. Bourgon isn't present, but a Defence lawyer is present, and naturally he will represent the accused. We hope that Mr. Bourgon will be arriving shortly. Mr. Withopf, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution has strong concerns to proceed. Defence counsel for the accused Hadzihasanovic is not in the courtroom. The person who is in the courtroom is a legal assistant to Defence counsel. I think it's not appropriate to continue with the examination-in-chief of Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Dixon, where is your colleague?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am not sure where he is at the moment. He was in the Defence room a moment ago, and inquiries were made as to where he was. Perhaps if a telephone call could be made, Your Honour, he could be located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will try to find him -- here he is. We were waiting for you, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. I was in the building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, I do apologise for the break. This was for technical reasons, obviously. Sir Martin, I understand that you still have in front of you the ECMM report of the 29th of October, 1993, and you were about for the benefit of the Trial Chamber to explain what the abbreviations do mean.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I could just repeat. At the top, HQ Zagreb is the headquarters of the ECMM, and the HUM stands for the "humanitarian cell." Coordinating centre Mostar; coordinating centre Tuzla. And the ECLO Kiseljak stands for the EC liaison officer in Kiseljak, which was then the headquarters of UNPROFOR, just down the road. V2 Gornji Vakuf is the team Victor 2, one of the four teams of CC Travnik based down in Gornji Vakuf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Sir Martin. If I may now please draw your attention to page 1, under paragraph 1. There is a heading "Political," and then there is a second paragraph which starts with "V1." Can you please tell the Trial Chamber for what "V1" stands for.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: V1 or Victor 1 was the team of CC Travnik based -- or covering the Vitez-Busovaca-Travnik area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you, Sir Martin, please could have a look at the very last lines, the three last lines of this paragraph, which read "... but suggested that Mujahedin units could have been there and he would not know because they reported directly to 3 Corps BiH." Sir Martin, is this statement in the ECMM report in line with what you told us about your conversations and discussions with Hadzihasanovic about the subordination of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My understanding always was that the Mujahedin were theoretically under the command of 3 Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The Prosecution wishes to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have no objections, but we would like to make a correction as far as the identification of the document on the list is concerned. The document at the moment has the number P178, marked for identification, and it says "The European Community Monitoring Mission, RC Zenica [as interpreted], Daily Summary." The date is the 29th of October. And the document in question here is a report that comes from the coordination centre of Travnik. So we would like a correction to be made as far as the title of the document is concerned. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This document comes from the coordination centre. It will be recorded in the transcript. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: No objection with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, could we have an exhibit number for all three versions, the B/C/S version, the English version, and the French one. [In English] 178.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the English version gets exhibit number P178; the B/C/S translation gets the exhibit number P178/BCS; and the French translation gets the exhibit number P178/F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Can the witness please keep this report, since we need it at a later stage of the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, do you know an individual with the name Asim Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Asim Fazlic, yes, he was the chief of police in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time, Sir Martin, when you discussed the issue of subordination of the Mujahedin with Mr. Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In one of the meetings that I had with him, we did discuss that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you still recall what Mr. Fazlic told you about the subordination of the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Fazlic during that meeting said that the Mujahedin were under the command of 3 Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: With the permission of the Trial Chamber, I'm now going to show the witness a further document. It's the ECMM report of 6 January 1994. It has been marked for identification with P230 by a decision of the Trial Chamber of 2nd of April. This document is also not contested by Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, if I may, please, draw your attention to page 3 and page 4, and on page 3 to paragraph 4, and on page 4 to the first paragraph, which starts with the word "comment." Can you please first tell the Trial Chamber for what the abbreviation HRC, at the beginning of paragraph 4, stands for.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: HRC stands for "head of the regional centre," which was me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please, Sir Martin, have a look at the last paragraph on page 3, which starts with the words "On the subject of the Mujahedin ...." And the question is: Does what's written in this report, does it reflect the result of your conversation with Mr. Asim Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because this is a report written by myself -- no, it's actually signed by the operations officer. But I am quite sure that I would have produced that input, because it was the meeting that I had attended.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle of this paragraph, it reads: "He stated clearly that they were all under the command of 3 BiH Corps." And there he's making reference to the Mujahedin. Can you confirm today, Sir Martin, that Mr. Asim Fazlic made such a statement?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because I read this report immediately after the meeting, that evening, and I would have taken notes, and so that is what he clearly said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, at the time you met with Mr. Fazlic and you discussed this very same issue with him, at the time and in respect to the issues discussed, what were your views on Mr. Fazlic's professionalism and reliability?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was impressed by Fazlic. He was young, I'd say about 35; dynamic. And I thought him a thoroughly professional police officer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I please in this context, Sir Martin, draw your attention to the first paragraph on page 4, which starts with the word "Comment." It reads: "Fazlic is a young dynamic chief of police who laughs a lot and gives the impression of being thoroughly professional and determined in his duties. He also appears genuine." It makes a statement about the Mujahedin being under the command of 3 BiH Corps: "... most interesting - as that was certainly not the impression given by Alagic." Sir Martin, is this your comment?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my comment, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it still today your view on Mr. Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my view of Mr. Fazlic, and I've had no reason in the ensuing years to change my view because I've never seen or heard of Mr. Fazlic again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. -- thank you, Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The Prosecution wishes to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no objections to having this document admitted into evidence. Nevertheless, Mr. President, we'd like to make the same comment again. There are certain paragraphs in this document that haven't been referred to by the witness, but more importantly, the date of this document is the 6th of January, 1994 and that is beyond the ratione temporis referred to in the indictment. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have taken notes of your comments. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the English version gets the exhibit number P230; the B/C/S translation gets the exhibit number P230/BCS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, did you ever during the time you spent in Zenica meet an individual with the name Stipan Radic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Stipan Radic, he was the Franciscan priest in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever meet him?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had quite a number of meetings with him and had a high opinion of him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what, Sir Martin, was your high opinion of Stipan Radic based upon?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was looking after the remaining Croats in Zenica. He had a difficult job, and it was clear that he was a most-dedicated man. And if one can use the phrase, I would say he really was a man of God. He struck me as being a very good man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What sort of issues have you discussed with Stipan Radic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: We quite often discussed the problem of harassment of Croats by Bosniak soldiers, mainly on the villages on the outskirts of Zenica in the direction of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whenever, Sir Martin, you discussed the issues you just explained to us with Stipan Radic, how would you assess his reliability in the sense whether his statements turned out to be true or not?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did turn out to be true because when they were followed up by the Bosniak commanders, they accepted that there was a problem and invariably there was an improvement in the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand, Sir Martin, you still have in front of you the ECMM report of 3 November 1993, which is Prosecution Exhibit P181.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may, please, draw your attention, Sir Martin, to pages 5 and 6. On page 5, to paragraphs 2, 3, and 4; and on page 6, to paragraph 5. Please take your time to read it carefully.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you said paragraphs 2 and 3 on -- paragraph 5 -- on page 5?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And then on page 5, there starts paragraph 4 --

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4 and 5.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. And then paragraph 5 on page 6.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please take your time to read it carefully.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, this portion of this report is headed by "Meeting between HOM and Father Stipan Radic," and some others, obviously. And if I do recall correctly, you were HOM; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was HRC. The HOM was the head of mission, who was the Ambassador De Baans. But I was present at this meeting, I -- I'm pretty sure I must have been present. Yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you were present at this meeting with Father Stipan Radic, is what's written under paragraphs 2 to 5, is it correctly reflected in the report what has been discussed?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a correct reflection of the -- of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this statement, Sir Martin, also apply to the content of paragraph 4, which is partially on page 5 and partially on page 6?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution wishes -- I think we already tendered it into evidence. It's Prosecution Exhibit P181.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, I'm now moving on to a different matter. Were you ever been informed about the kidnapping of Croats in Travnik?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a particular -- I think I -- this incident came to a head sometime in December, when I was informed of a Croat called Adzaip who had been kidnapped by the Mujahedin. I was informed this by the Victor 1 team from Travnik, and the story was that Adzaip had been converted to Islam by the Mujahedin and then had been let out for some "leave" and then decided that he did not want to go back and therefore was very fearful for his life, frightened of the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get to know who was responsible for the kidnapping of Mr. Adzaip and other Croats?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was -- to my mind, there was no doubt that it was the Mujahedin, and I think it was -- well, General Alagic was in command at the time, and he certainly did not deny that it was the Mujahedin who were responsible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this context of Croats being kidnapped by Mujahedin, did you get to know about an individual with the family name Popovic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I received a letter. I knew that he was one of the four -- of that particular four who had been kidnapped. And then I received a letter from Popovic's wife -- Dragoljub, I think his name was, Dragoljub Popovic -- from his wife, Liljana, asking me to -- said that her husband had been missing since October and asking me to do what I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after, Sir Martin, after you had received that letter, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had more than one meeting with General Alagic, who was then commander of 3 Corps. He expressed himself very concerned about the matter. He said he knew the Popovic family and he would do what he could to find out what had happened to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you get to know what he actually found out?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think my last letter back to Mrs. Popovic telling her that I had not been able to find out was probably in January. I can't remember exactly. But to my great regret, by the time I left Zenica in April, I still had not found out then what had happened to Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you are referring to a letter to Mrs. Popovic, Sir Martin, can the witness be -- please be provided with the letter of 1st January 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: For the information of the Trial Chamber and the Defence, this letter is marked for identification as P182 by a decision of the Trial Chamber of 2nd of April, and it's obviously a document not contested by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, I understand you have the letter in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the letter you were referring to a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, that is the letter I wrote to Mrs. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It makes reference to meetings with General Alagic. Is this reference correct?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, those are the meetings which I referred to a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the Prosecution wishes to tender this letter into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Registrar, can we -- just a moment. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. No objection to this document being admitted. It was obviously written by the witness. Nevertheless, we would like to point out that the letter is dated the 1st of January, 1994, for the benefit of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon? Very well. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours exhibit number P183, and -- P182, and the B/C/S translation gets exhibit number P182/BCS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Withopf, continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this very same context, Sir Martin - and I understand you still have in front of you the ECMM report of the 29th of October, 1993 -

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please have a look at page 2, the second paragraph, which starts with "V1" - Victor 1 - and can you please read it carefully.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you've been in Zenica, did you become aware of this meeting and what has been discussed with Alagic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- I think I was aware, but I am afraid I did not get involved in this particular business about the hostages until Victor 1 came to see me in connection with Adzaip and Popovic. In other words, I was not directly involved on the 29th of October.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this portion of the document, however, does it reflect what you have been informed about at a later point in time?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, I also understand that you still have the ECMM report of 6 January 1994 in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I now, please, draw your attention at page 3 at the very bottom. More specifically, at the last four lines, which read as follows: "When asked about the 'Mujahedin' at Mehurici, where Popovic and the other three who were seized by the 'Mujahedin' were held, he said that this force was also under the command of 3 BiH Corps." The person who said this is obviously Mr. Asim Fazlic.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please confirm today that this was told to you by Mr. Asim Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. As I say, this is a report actually signed by the operations officer, but this section would have been inserted by me, as it was I who attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: And can the witness in the very same context now please be provided, with the permission of the Trial Chamber, of the ECMM report of 4 November 1993. For the information of the Trial Chamber and the Defence, this document is marked for identification following the decision of the Trial Chamber of 2nd of April as P198. The English original, the B/C/S, and the French translations are available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, can you please first identify who was responsible for drafting this report.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is signed by William Stutt, the head of the coordinating centre Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I please, Sir Martin, draw your attention to page 3 of this report, and in particular to the short paragraph under 6, which is headed with "Other matters."

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this paragraph is written: "Meanwhile, he will attempt to assist with the problem of hostages taken by Mujahedin in Travnik." And the person who is referred to is obviously Commander Alagic.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this statement in the report reflect what you got to know about Alagic's involvement in this issue?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. -- Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: The Prosecution, Mr. President, Your Honours, wishes to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence has no objection to the admission of this document; however, the Defence would like to note that the witness answered a moment ago that he was not personally involved in this type of event and also that he learnt about these things later. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the English version gets the exhibit number P198; the B/C/S translation gets the exhibit number P198/BCS; and the French translation gets the exhibit number P198/F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Dixon -- I'm sorry, Mr. Withopf, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, we are now moving on to another subject. Did you get to know whether ABiH units took over Vares?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I got to know -- I think it was the very day that it happened, which as far as I can remember was about the 3rd of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please, Sir Martin, inform the Trial Chamber as to how you got to know about it.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed about it by the head of the coordinating centre Travnik, who'd -- he'd received the reports from his team Victor 4 which covered that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: I understand, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The Trial Chamber will adjourn at five to 12.00 because there will be one minute of silence. We will resume -- so at 12.00 it is necessary to have one minutes' silence. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, you were just informing us that you were informed about the situation in Vares by the head of the coordination centre Travnik. What did he actually inform you about?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: That the Bosniak -- the ABiH had seized Vares and the Croat - the HVO - had fled, and that the ABiH were in control of Vares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you yourself, Sir Martin, did you go to Vares?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went up -- I heard about this I think in the evening. The following day I went up to Vares with William Stutt, the head of the coordinating centre Travnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall the date as to when you arrived in Vares?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am pretty sure it was the 4th of November.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 4th of November, 1993 or --

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4th of November, 1993, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you arrived in Vares, what was the military situation about?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was clear that the ABiH were in control, although there were some very extraordinary scenes going on. I likened it at the time to Dodge City in the Wild West because there were soldiers, ABiH soldiers who appeared to be drunk going around shooting their weapons. I called it "slivovitz shooting," not firing at any enemy but firing into the air in a pretty dangerous manner. There was a lot of damage, broken windows, smashed-in doors, but it was not possible to say whether that had been done by the ABiH or it had been done by the withdrawing HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were just saying, Sir Martin, "by the withdrawing HVO." Having seen Vares immediately after the takeover by the ABiH, did you get the impression that Vares was defended by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- my reckoning was they had decided to move out without putting up a fight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also mentioning that you have seen ABiH units in Vares on the 4th of November, 1993. Are you in a position to detail which units, ABiH units you have seen?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly -- certainly as we approached on the outskirts of Vares, it was the 7th Muslim Brigade. But -- so all the soldiers within Vares, I couldn't identify them by units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 7th Muslim Brigade soldiers on the outskirts of Vares, --

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- how were you able to identify them as 7th Muslim Brigade soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I clearly identified them as Muslim Brigade. I can only think that it was insignia they were wearing on their shoulders specific to 7 Muslim Brigade. Certainly we did identify them as 7 Muslim Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were mentioning earlier on, Sir Martin, that you arrived in Vares on the 4th of November, 1993. Do you still have a recollection as to when, what time during the day?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we went up fairly early. It took about an hour, an hour and a half to get up to Vares, so my guess is it was probably half past 9.00, 10.00, that sort of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I'm close to finishing the examination-in-chief; however, I have a document to show to the witness, and it will certainly take another five minutes or so. I would therefore suggest to have the short break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we'll have the break, as I announced. It is now nine minutes to noon. We will have a break, and we will resume at five past 12.00. And I would like to ask those who remain in this courtroom to observe a minute of silence at noon, as has been requested for all the buildings within the UN family. So we will have a break and resume at five past 12.00. --- Break taken at 11.52 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir Martin, a small point for clarification. You earlier on mentioned that you arrived in Vares on the 4th of November, 1993 in the evening. Just prior to the break, you informed us, asked about the time, "probably half past 9.00, 10.00, that sort of time." For clarification only, was it in the evening or in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't recall saying previously that I'd arrived in the evening. I said I'd heard about it in the evening and decided to go up the following morning with William Stutt. So the fact that I went up in the evening is not correct. I heard about it in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to make it absolutely clear, you arrived in Vares at about 9.00 or 10.00 in the morning of the 4th of November, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my memory, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Sir Martin, I understand you still have in front of you the ECMM report of 4 November 1993, which is Prosecution Exhibit P198.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you, Sir Martin, please have a look at the first page and at the first page at paragraph 1, which has the heading "General situation Vares," and can you read it for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this paragraph and its contents, does it reflect what you yourself have seen in Vares on the 4th of November, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARTIN GARROD [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. The report was written by William Stutt, who of course we were together, and it does reflect the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Sir Martin.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, this concludes the Prosecution's examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Withopf. As the Defence has already told us - but I would like this to be confirmed - they will cross-examine the witness at a subsequent date. Is that correct, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In fact, the Defence would like to cross-examine the witness, Sir Martin Garrod, at a subsequent date. Nevertheless, Mr. President, at this point in time the Defence would like to express the fact that it regrets that it cannot cross-examine Sir Martin Garrod today for two reasons: Firstly, because Sir Martin Garrod will have to come back to The Hague; and also, Mr. President, we regret that we can't clarify -- we're not in a position to clarify certain parts of Mr. Garrod's testimony today and so that this could enable the Trial Chamber to assess all the details of Mr. Garrod's testimony. We would like to express our gratitude to the witness, Sir Martin Garrod who agreed to meet us on Monday evening to enable us to prepare ourselves. Since his testimony has started, we can't meet him again before the beginning of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, simply to confirm what Mr. Bourgon has said; nothing further from the part of Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Sir Martin Garrod, the Trial Chamber would like to thank you for having testified. We'd like to thank you for the first part of your testimony that you gave within the framework of the examination-in-chief. You have understood that because of disclosure of certain exhibits the Defence wants to be in a position to conduct an efficient cross-examination, and as a result you will have to return to The Hague. We don't know when yet, but naturally the Prosecution will try to fix a date with you and they will try to find a date that won't pose a problem for you. Within the framework of these proceedings, which consist of an examination-in-chief and cross-examination, it is customary for the witness not to meet the parties after the beginning of the examination-in-chief. So you should no longer meet either of the parties now. You should just wait to be informed of the date when you should return. If you're not able to return, you should let us know, because if you can't, that's not your fault. Naturally, the Trial Chamber wishes you a safe trip home, and naturally we would like to thank you for having come here and testified before the Tribunal. I will now ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Withopf, I am listening to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: In respect as to when Sir Martin is expected to be back, there are two opportunities; however, Sir Martin first has to consult his agenda. It would be either the 27th of April or the 12th of May. For the sake of the transcript, a very small issue I wish to emphasise, since Sir Martin is under oath, any contacts, even in respect to the scheduling of his cross-examination, will be made via the Victims and Witness Section. The Prosecution will certainly not get in contact with Sir Martin. I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Naturally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence has taken note of the dates, the 27th of April or the 12th of May. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We were informed of these two dates yesterday. These two dates suit us. But I'd like to inform you that we would like to cross-examine this witness for a period that should probably be about 50 per cent more than the period used up by the Prosecution. According to the figures that we have, the examination-in-chief took about 1 hour and 15 minutes, and we will probably want to examine the witness -- cross-examine the witness for two hours. This should make it possible for the Prosecution to compile its schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That's not a problem. The second stage of this hearing was supposed to be held tomorrow, but we can deal with this matter today. This debate will consist of two stages. We have to give numbers to noncontested documents; and secondly, we have to give numbers to documents which will be tendered by the Prosecution pursuant to Rule 92 bis. Naturally there was also the question of contested documents. We said that these documents would be marked for identification, they would be given a temporary number. But given that we don't have copies of these documents, we will give them temporary numbers on Monday, the 19th of April, when we resume with our hearings. It's necessary for us to adjourn for a few minutes so that the registrar can go and collect the documents. The registrar will need 15 minutes to deal with this. It is now quarter past 12.00. We will resume at half past 12.00 to deal with this matter. We should be finished very quickly, since we have uncontested documents with provisional numbers. So we have 19 documents pursuant to Rule 92 bis which require numbers. So we will resume at half past 12.00. --- Break taken at 12.17 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing is resumed. The registrar told me that he had some problems with the computer but he'll manage with the means at his disposal to respond to the concerns of the Chamber regarding the admission into evidence of certain documents. As I noted a moment ago, we have two matters to deal with: First of all, the admission of noncontested documents which were listed in an annex that you had, as it was attached to our ruling of the 2nd of April, 2004; then we have documents that were marked for identification, beginning with P120 and which go on up until P382. Regarding these documents, Mr. Withopf, that were marked for identification, what do you have to tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, these documents were marked for identification mainly for the reason because Defence for the accused did not contest such documents being admitted into evidence. Accordingly, the Prosecution today requests these documents, as detailed in the annex to Your Honours' 2nd of April decision, to be tendered into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I now turn to Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. During our written submission filed last Monday, we conveyed to the Chamber that we have no objection regarding the admissibility of these documents. However, in those same submissions, Mr. President, we conveyed certain remarks regarding the probative value of those documents. We are of the opinion that if those documents are not supported by other evidence, be it through oral testimony of a witness, another document, or other elements which may be produced by the Prosecution, that in that case the documents as such should be given minimum probative value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. To confirm on behalf of Mr. Kubura, there's no objection to any of those documents being admitted and accordingly in our submission those documents can now be admitted as part of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's fine. Mr. Registrar, these documents which are listed in an annex beginning with P120 going on up until P382, will you please confirm that their numbers now become final exhibit numbers and when the computer starts working again, you will do what is necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, all the documents listed in annex of the decision of the 2nd of April, 2004 which are not yet admitted are considered to be admitted now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now let us address the other item on our agenda, and that is the testimony collected through 92 bis statements. Unless I am mistaken, we have 19 such statements. The witnesses begin with Mr. Baric and the nineteenth on my list is Mr. Vrvilo, according to the alphabetical order. Mr. Withopf.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we please go into private session, since obviously names of witnesses will be mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let us go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 19th day of April, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.59 p.m.,
